groups.title: HTML Semantics & Accessibility
groups.question: You are building the HTML for a blog article page that must work well with screen readers and search engines. Explain how you would structure it.

followUps.Semantic HTML Elements: Why do elements like article, nav and main matter?
followUps.ARIA and Accessibility Tree: What is the accessibility tree, and how can ARIA misuse hurt it?

evidence.text: Semantic elements describe what each part of the page is.
Screen readers use them to let users jump between regions.
Search engines use the structure to understand the content.

notEnough: Only saying semantic HTML is cleaner.

evidence.text: The accessibility tree is what screen readers read, built from the DOM.
Images need alt text so their meaning appears there.
Wrong ARIA roles give users false information, which is worse than none.

groups.title: CSS Layout Fundamentals
groups.question: Your blog's cards overflow their columns and the page layout is built with hacks. Explain the box model and modern layout tools.

followUps.CSS Box Model: Why does adding padding make a fixed-width card overflow?
followUps.Flexbox and Grid: When would you use flexbox and when grid?

evidence.text: Every element is a box of content, padding, border and margin.
By default, width covers only the content, so padding is added on top.
border-box includes padding and border in the width.
Flexbox lays items out in one direction.
Grid controls rows and columns at the same time.
Grid suits page and card layouts; flexbox suits rows of items like navigation.

notEnough: Only saying one is 1D and one is 2D.

groups.title: TypeScript Type System
groups.question: You are adding TypeScript to an Astro project and defining the shape of blog post data. Explain how TypeScript helps.

followUps.Static Typing and Type Inference: What does static typing catch, and when should you annotate rather than rely on inference?
followUps.Interfaces and Type Aliases: When would you use an interface and when a type alias?

evidence.text: TypeScript catches type errors before the code runs.
It infers many types from values.
Function parameters and public boundaries should be annotated explicitly.
Both describe object shapes.
Interfaces can be extended and merged.
Type aliases can describe unions and intersections.

groups.title: Responsive Design
groups.question: Your blog looks good on desktop but breaks on phones, and the brand color is hard-coded in 50 places. Explain how you would make it responsive and themeable.

followUps.CSS Custom Properties: How do CSS custom properties help with theming?

evidence.text: Base styles target small screens.
min-width media queries add changes for larger screens.
This usually produces less CSS than undoing a desktop layout.

notEnough: Only saying you use media queries.

evidence.text: Values like colors and spacing are defined once as variables.
Variables cascade, so changing them on a parent updates everything inside.
Switching variable values switches the theme without rewriting CSS.
